newsitem.title: BURKINA FASO: Burkina Faso students resume strike.
newsitem.headline: Burkina Faso students resume strike.

text.p: Students in Burkina Faso began a new 72-hour strike on Thursday following a breakdown in talks with the government on grievances over grants, allowances and conditions, student activists said.
A meeting of over 1,000 students at the university in the capital Ouagadougou called on the government to provide concrete responses to their demands before the end of the latest strike.
The students began a series of strikes on January 29 but suspended their action on Monday after the government released detained student leaders and activists.
Talks between the two sides on Wednesday collapsed after the students rejected as inadequate the proposed creation of an ad hoc commission to study their grievances.

The National Association of Burkinabe Students called the strikes over demands ranging from allowances for students not on formal grants to cheaper bus fares, improved food in the university restaurant and help with health expenses.

The government said it had decided to free the students after numerous calls from trades unions and society at large for action to defuse the crisis. They were detained after the initial strike call and clashes with security forces.

In neighbouring Ivory Coast a five-day strike called by the student federation FESCI from Wednesday to secure the release of detained activists and to protest over grants and conditions has virtually brought university classes to a standstill.
